headline: A strong Thanksgiving storm brings 1 to 3 inches of rain (heaviest on the Olympic Peninsula), damaging winds through noon and coastal flooding along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound, before a lighter system Friday and a brief dry break Saturday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A strong storm system sweeps across western Washington on Thanksgiving, with a Wind Advisory until noon for the Eastern and Western Strait of Juan de Fuca, the Lake Crescent area along US 101, Port Townsend and the Puget Sound lowlands including Seattle; gusts run about 30 to 40 mph inland and about 45 to 50 mph on the coast and near Bellingham, where a High Wind Warning covers the coast until noon. The storm adds 1 to 3 inches of rain, most of it on the Olympic Peninsula and the coast, and the Bear Gulch burn scar on the Olympic Peninsula could see more small landslides. Rain turns to showers this afternoon behind a cold front, with a 15 to 25 percent chance of thunderstorms, and winds drop off noticeably this evening. Snow levels are high at 6,000 to 7,000 feet, but a Winter Storm Warning continues for the Whatcom and Skagit County Cascades until 4 AM Friday, and the Skokomish River stays in moderate flood this afternoon under a River Flood Warning through Friday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday is calmer, but a much weaker system brings light rain back across the area by Friday afternoon, without the heavy rain or strong winds. Saturday turns drier as a weak area of high pressure moves onshore, with temperatures back to near normal for the season. The Skokomish River should drop below flood stage Friday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The dry break is brief, with another storm system moving offshore Sunday, though computer models disagree widely on how it develops; one model run spins up a strong low pressure center offshore by Sunday night, which forecasters are watching because of holiday travel. Models continue to disagree into early next week, with a hint of another short dry break around Wednesday. For now the forecast calls for near-normal temperatures and a general chance of rain, typical for early December, and the Skokomish River could rise again.

coast: Coastal flooding is a major concern Thursday as high astronomical tides combine with storm surge and high surf, with impacts peaking on the inland waters today before tides gradually weaken. A Coastal Flood Warning runs from 10 AM to 6 PM Thursday for the Eastern and Western Strait of Juan de Fuca and the northern and Grays Harbor County coasts, a Coastal Flood Warning until 10 AM covers Puget Sound shorelines from Olympia to Whatcom County plus Hood Canal and the San Juan Islands, and Coastal Flood Advisories cover the Port Townsend area until 10 AM and the lower Chehalis River valley from 10 AM to 6 PM. Coastal Flood Watches follow for the San Juan Islands late Thursday night through Friday morning and the Grays Harbor County coast Friday. On the water, a Storm Warning covers the east entrance of the Strait of Juan de Fuca until 10 AM, with Gale Warnings on the coastal waters, the west entrance of the Strait, Admiralty Inlet and the northern inland waters until 10 AM and Puget Sound and Hood Canal until 7 AM, then Small Craft Advisories into Thursday evening; thunderstorms over the water could bring lightning, gusty winds and small hail. Ocean seas of 15 to 20 feet ease to 10 to 15 feet by Friday morning and below 10 feet this weekend, though a westerly push of wind is likely through the Strait this weekend, and seas rise above 10 feet again next week.
watch_for: Coastal flooding along the Strait of Juan de Fuca from 10 AM to 6 PM Thursday
Possible strong offshore storm Sunday night that could affect holiday travel
More small landslides on the Bear Gulch burn scar and renewed Skokomish River rises next week
confidence: Confidence is high in Thursday's storm and the lighter Friday system and brief dry Saturday, but low from Sunday into next week because computer models disagree on the next storms.
